name: Cold storage
summary: Refrigerated/freezer warehouses cost roughly 2–3× a dry warehouse: insulated metal panel (IMP) envelope, heated and insulated slab for freezer zones, an ammonia or CO2 refrigeration plant (25–35% of cost), insulated dock doors and much larger electrical service; many new builds are 40–50'+ clear for automated storage. Public evidence is thin — the available per-SF ranges are contractor/advisory articles — so the default is cross-checked bottom-up against the dry-warehouse baseline plus the specialty-MEP building blocks.

typicalSize.method: Terrapin lists typical cold-storage builds at 30k–200k SF (e5); modern 3PL/automated facilities run to 300–400k SF. Mid 175k SF (judgment).

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: FAR ~0.30–0.40 (truck courts with reefer plug-ins, engine-room yard, larger setbacks): 43,560 × 0.345 ≈ 15,000 SF/acre.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Same employee-parking ratio as dry distribution (0.3–1.0 per 1,000 SF).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Top-down: Terrapin cooler $150–$250 and freezer $200–$350 (e1/e2); a typical multi-temperature facility (≈40% cooler/dock, 60% freezer) blends to ≈ $180–$310, midpoint ≈ $245. Bottom-up check: dry big-box shell + sitework ≈ $110/SF (warehouse-distribution mid $100 + 10% for taller 40–50' clear and smaller size; C&W medium $87, e6) + refrigeration $55 (specialty-mep block mid; e3 $15–$60) + IMP envelope ≈ 1.4 SF of wall/ceiling panel per floor SF × $24 = $34 + sub-slab heating on 60% of floor × $11 = $7 + insulated doors, vapour/slab insulation and electrical service upgrade ≈ $25–$35 → ≈ $231–$241. Mid $240. Low $170 = cooler-dominant facility in a low-cost market (e1 midpoint-low); high $350 = top of freezer range (e2), consistent with Terrapin tilt-up cold shell $215–$325 (e5) once MEP is added. Blast/ultra-low facilities can exceed this.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. GC/OH&P, shell, IMP envelope, heated slab in freezer zones, refrigeration plant and distribution, insulated docks, electrical service and typical sitework (reefer truck courts). Excludes ASRS/racking/material handling, land, soft costs, utility off-sites (substation/line extensions) and fees.

qualityTiers.method: economy ≈ low/mid (cooler-only); premium ≈ high/mid (freezer-dominant, 1.46) tempered to 1.3; luxury 1.6 ≈ blast-freeze/ultra-low share (Terrapin blast $280–$450, e2) or high-bay automated facility.

systemSplit.method: Refrigeration (23) 22% ≈ lower end of the 25–35% refrigeration share (e4, specialty-mep e2) because some refrigeration electrical sits in 26. IMP insulated enclosure carried in 13 (11%) + 07 roofing (4%) ≈ $36/SF at mid, matching the bottom-up envelope check. Heated/insulated slab inflates 03. Pre-action/dry sprinklers in freezers (21) 4%. Sitework smaller share than dry warehouse because building cost is higher. Judgment — verify.

cost.method: From _blocks/specialty-mep.json cold-storage-refrigeration ($30/$55/$90 per SF): Pulse RevOps $30–$90/SF and 25–35% of a $175–$275/SF frozen facility; Terrapin $15–$60/SF (e3) brackets the cooler end.

lineItems.name: Insulated metal panel walls & ceiling (per SF of floor; ~1.4 SF panel per SF)

cost.method: From _blocks/specialty-mep.json freezer-insulated-envelope ($15/$24/$35 per SF of panel): Terrapin IMP $12–$35/SF, freezer walls $18–$30/SF. Quantity 1.4 SF of panel per floor SF ≈ 200k SF box, 45–50 ft high (perimeter walls ≈ 0.45 SF/SF + insulated ceiling 1.0 SF/SF).

lineItems.name: Freezer sub-slab heating & insulation (freezer zones)

cost.method: From _blocks/specialty-mep.json freezer-subslab-heating ($8/$11/$15 per SF): Terrapin $8–$12/SF sub-slab heating; "+$8–$18/SF for heated slab" (e3). Quantity = freezer share of floor area, assumed 60%.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out; set qty to 0 for cooler-only buildings.

lineItems.name: Blast-freeze cells (optional, per SF of cell)

cost.method: Premium over freezer space: Terrapin blast freeze $280–$450 vs freezer $200–$350 (e2) → +$80–$100/SF at the range ends; high adds dedicated low-temp compressors/evaporators (judgment). Quantity: 5% of building area.

lineItems.name: Utility service / switchgear upsizing for refrigeration load

cost.method: No public source fetched. A 175k SF freezer facility draws ~3–6 MW vs <1 MW for dry; medium-voltage switchgear, transformers and backup for refrigeration controls ≈ $0.5M–$2.5M (judgment). Off-site utility line extensions excluded.

pctOfHard.method: Dry-warehouse soft costs (10–20%) applied to a 2–3× larger hard cost, so A/E and permits fall as a percentage, offset by refrigeration engineering, ammonia PSM/RMP compliance and commissioning: 11–19%, mid 14% (judgment).

softCosts.notes: Type-specific soft items: refrigeration design-build engineering, ammonia process safety management (PSM) and risk management plan (RMP) if >10,000 lb NH3, commissioning/pull-down energy.

design.method: Refrigeration and automation integration add design risk (judgment).

hard.method: Long-lead refrigeration/electrical equipment and panel supply risk → 5–10% (judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: min ≈ hard low $170 × 1.03 (cooler-only, lean soft); max ≈ blast-freeze-heavy facility at Terrapin's $450 top (e2) × 1.07.

openQuestions: All per-SF evidence is from contractor/advisory articles; obtain a cost-consultant or REIT (Americold/Lineage) disclosure of cost per SF or per pallet position.
Confirm whether Terrapin zone ranges include sitework (the article says yes, but also lists site work separately at $12–$35/SF).
Consider a per-pallet-position or per-cubic-foot unit for automated high-bay facilities.
